pointers.text: Use printed FBT base (inc GST) if nonzero. If $0, add retail, options and delivery, subtract discounts, then add GST. Confirm.
pointers.more: ORIX incorrectly prints $0 as the FBT base value on some reviewed EV quotes. An FBT exemption does not make the car's cost-based FBT base value zero; a notional taxable value is still calculated for reportable benefits. If the discount is printed as a negative amount, add it with its minus sign instead; do not subtract twice. The pictured car-price rows are ex GST: multiply their net amount by 1.10, and exclude stamp duty and registration/CTP. Ask ORIX to confirm your estimate.

pointers.text: No total printed? Add GST to the car-price rows, then add on-road costs. Confirm the result with ORIX or the dealer.
pointers.more: Add retail price, options and dealer delivery, then subtract discounts. If the discount is printed as a negative amount, add it with its minus sign instead; do not subtract twice. Add GST if those rows are ex GST, then add stamp duty and registration/CTP. “GST not recoverable from Input Tax Credit” is in ORIX's capital cost, but the quote doesn't say whether it is part of the dealer's on-road price. Ask ORIX where it belongs and count it only once. “Capital cost for Vehicle Lease” is an ex-GST financing figure, not the drive-away total.
